Subject: Exhibit B redline (runtime carveouts) attached

Kimberly —

Thanks for the time yesterday. Attached is our redline to Exhibit B that narrows runtime access and telemetry collection. The key requests are:
- No outbound subprocessor exports of inference-level KV cache snapshots.
- Explicit prohibition on using inference outputs for training without prior consent.
- Retention caps of 30 days for telemetry related to customer tokens.

We flagged a carveout that would allow runtime debugging dumps to a secure S3 bucket in certain emergency cases — see §4.2. Please loop in your product/security contacts; we need to understand if these are acceptable for a pilot.

Attachments: ACME_ExhibitB_redline_v3.pdf

Kim / team —

We reviewed ACME's redline and the matrix. High-level security stance:
- No outbound KV cache exports: acceptable as a standard prohibition. However, we need to preserve a narrow, auditable emergency path for dumps tied to a support ticket and signed-off by two managers (SRE + CISO delegate). We propose language that permits "temporary, encrypted, access-restricted diagnostic exports" limited to X requests per year and requiring downstream deletion confirmation.
- "No training on inference outputs": this is reasonable, but we will need an operational definition of "inference outputs" vs. aggregated telemetry. Product must define what falls into each bucket (examples: raw tokens, masked logs, error traces).
- 30-day telemetry retention: acceptable for token-level telemetry but may break some observability alerts which rely on 90-day baselines. We can support 30 days for customer-identifiable telemetry while keeping aggregated, anonymized metrics for longer.

Open items for product: please provide the canonical classification (raw output, derivative metric, aggregated telemetry) and a short mapping to how our runtime currently stores each item. Once that's done, Security can draft suggested contract language for the emergency dump workflow and the definition of training prohibition.

- Olga (Security, Product Security Engineer)

From: dev_patel@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Fwd: Exhibit B redline (runtime carveouts) attached

Quick product input following Olga's ask —
1) Classification:
- Inference outputs: full-response text produced by the model (per-request payloads).
- Derivative telemetry: latency, token counts, error traces, model-selection logs (non-customer-content).
- Debug dumps: KV cache snapshots, full request+response bundles pulled for debugging.

Current storage:
- We do not persist full per-request outputs in persistent storage by default; streaming responses are ephemeral. Exceptions: customers who opt-in to extended logging or who run Dedicated/Private with configured retention.
- Aggregated metrics are retained for 180 days by default in our analytics pipeline (anonymized).
- We support ad-hoc, encrypted debug exports for SRE-led investigations, but they require ticketing and deletion workflows; those exports are not enabled by default for hosted customers.

Proposed contract language bullets:
- Define "inference outputs" as above and prohibit model training on any stored inference outputs unless the customer has explicitly opted in in writing.
- Allow encrypted, time-limited diagnostic exports with two-person approval and mandatory audit logs; cap to 6 exports/year per customer unless higher threshold approved by CISO.
- Retention: support 30-day retention for customer-identifiable telemetry; keep aggregated anonymized metrics for internal product analytics.

If Security is good with these bullets, I can draft the counter-redline for Exhibit B.

— Dev (Product Manager, Runtime)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Exhibit B redline (runtime carveouts) — Redwood internal signoff and proposal

Lisa / ACME team —

Thanks for the redline and patience while we pulled internal feedback. Summary of Redwood's proposed counterpoints (see attached redline v3b):
1) Training prohibition: we accept a prohibition on training using stored inference outputs. We will also add explicit language that customers may opt in to a separate, mutually agreed process for contributing outputs for model-improvement programs.
2) Debugging/export carveout: we can support temporary, encrypted debug exports limited to 6 events/year per account (emergency threshold) with two-person authorization (SRE + Security delegate), KMS encryption, and mandatory deletion confirmation. We will add audit log language and a requirement for a joint incident post-mortem for any export.
3) Retention windows: we agree to 30-day retention for identifiable telemetry. Redwood will maintain aggregated, anonymized metrics for internal analytics up to 180 days.

Next steps:
- ACME legal to review these bullets and confirm whether 6/year and two-person approval meet your needs or if you require a different cap/workflow.
- If acceptable, we'll produce a marked Exhibit B (ACME_ExhibitB_redline_v3b.pdf) and request signature routing.

Attachments: ACME_ExhibitB_redline_v3b.pdf, runtime-data-scope-matrix.xlsx
